subject: Subprocessor export paths, processing countries, and minimal-privilege attestation
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@primeloans.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@primeloans.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: full subprocessor breakdown + export paths for PrimeLoans security review

Hi Ava,

We're running a security and privacy intake for our upcoming integration and my review flagged the need for a detailed subprocessor roster and explicit export/egress paths for any cross-border processing. Can you send: 
- A complete list of subprocessors (name, role, countries where they process data)
- Which processors handle keys/KMS/HSM and where key material resides
- Any temporary or transit processors used for logs/metrics and whether they see PII
- High-level data flow diagram or map showing where customer data crosses borders
- A short attestation that each subprocessor is limited to minimal privileges and that we have contractual obligations in place (or indicate where an addendum/DPA amendment is needed)

We have a tight window for our vendor review—ideally we can clear this with the infosec team by next week.

Thanks,
Oliver Grant
Senior Security Analyst, PrimeLoans
oliver.grant@primeloans.com

--
Attachment: none in this initial request
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: full subprocessor breakdown + export paths for PrimeLoans security review

Hi Oliver,

Thanks for the clear list — attaching what should cover the security intake. Quick summary inline below, and please see attached CSV and data flow diagram for full detail.

Summary (high level):
- Serving/runtime: KeyServe Inc. (US) — model inference and request routing; processes in us-west and eu-west regions.
- GPU infra: RackScale (US/DE) — reserved compute for Dedicated customers.
- Observability/metrics: LogStream Analytics (IE) — processes metrics and aggregated logs; does not receive raw prompts.
- Caching/edge: EdgeLight (US/AU) — KV prefix caching for latency; cached content limited to non-PII prefixes, see CSV.
- Key management: KeySecure Ltd. (US) — KMS for host encryption; HSM-backed keys for customer master keys when requested.

Notes on export/egress paths:
- Customer input and model outputs are stored/transited in region where configured; for Hosted, default is us-west.
- Where cross-border transfer occurs we use TLS 1.3, and backups are encrypted with KMS keys in the region unless customer requests key pinning.

Attestation:
- Each named subprocessor operates under Redwood's DPA terms and a subprocessor addendum; we've included a minimal-privilege attestation (PDF) that outlines role-limited access.

If you need a formal DPA amendment with explicit subprocessor list embedded, Kimberly is cc'd and can produce a draft to sign.

Attaching:
- subprocessor_breakdown_20270502.csv (role, country, processing notes)
- data_flow_diagram_v2.png (high-level flows + region labels)

Let us know if you want the CSV in an alternate format or if your auditors need additional evidence (logs, SOC2 mapping).

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.inference.com

Subject: Re: Request: full subprocessor breakdown + export paths for PrimeLoans security review

Hi Oliver — quick technical follow-up echos Ava's summary. A couple clarifications you may want to flag to your team: 

1) EdgeLight (caching) — they only hold hashed prefixes for routing and latency heuristics. We never store full prompt text in the edge caches; retention for those keys is ephemeral (< 24 hrs) by default.

2) LogStream Analytics — they receive aggregated event telemetry (request counts, 95th pct latency buckets) and anonymized error traces. If you require strict no-log access, we can operate under a temporary egress filter for your tenant.

3) KMS/HSM — KeySecure Ltd. provides HSM-backed CMKs for customers that request dedicated keys; in that configuration keys never leave the HSM and key material is generated and stored in-region (US or EU).

Attached is a short attestation we use internally describing minimal privileges and operator access windows. If your team needs signed timestamped evidence, Kimberly can route that as part of the DPA addendum process.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Staff Infra Engineer — Serving Runtime
jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com
[Attachment: minimal_privilege_attestation.pdf (PDF, 6KB)]

Oliver —

If PrimeLoans requires the subprocessor roster embedded in contract text, we can produce a DPA addendum. Draft language suggestions: 
- Subprocessor roster is Appendix A and will be updated with 30 days notice for additions.
- Transfers: Redwood will maintain encryption in transit and at rest; customer may request key pinning or HSM-backed CMKs.
- Audit: Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II reports and reasonable evidence for subprocessors upon written request; for direct audits we can scope a limited remote audit with coordination.
- Retention: default logs retention is 90 days; requestable retention profiles exist for Dedicated/Private deployments.

I attached a draft addendum for your review; if these items look fine we can generate a DocuSign envelope and include the current subprocessor CSV as Appendix A.

Thanks for the quick turnaround on this.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
